title: Modern LaTeX Editions of Public-Domain Mathematics Manuscripts
description:
This record is the public front page and bulk-preservation lane for an ongoing open project to produce modern, inspectable LaTeX editions and translation drafts of older mathematics and physics manuscripts. The durable reader files and large provenance files live on Zenodo; the GitHub mirror is used for coordination, issue reports, pull requests, current manifests, and lightweight source snapshots where practical.

How to read this archive. The project is not one uniform pile of OCR and it is not a set of certified critical editions. OCR converted to TeX, formula OCR, crops, and locator files are witness layers for checking and repair. The main scholarly value is in organized reader PDFs, TeX sources, source witnesses, repair ledgers, and translation drafts that can be checked and improved. File counts, upload size, and old progress-bar style labels are not completion metrics and do not imply source certification.

Open these first: best current reader/translation surfaces. The strongest public reader lanes are currently Noether, Weber, Frobenius, Kneser, Sylvester, and al-Battani. These records have coherent reader surfaces or work-level editions for declared scopes, but they remain working drafts rather than certified critical editions.

Serious source-aware work, caveat-heavy. SGA contains real SGA5 page-local repair work and substantial SGA6/SGA7 working translation/source-audit material. It is not OCR-only, but it is also not complete or globally source-faithful. SGA5 is controlled by its page-local workpass cursor; the latest compact promoted SGA5 delta remains p260-p265, while later local French workpass/provenance now reaches p480 in CERT_LOG.md and locally claims body-text completion for the selected 10-exposé SGA5 branch. That later evidence reports 52 TeX fixes, about 160 source-documented items, D001-D193 diagram tracking, and a 306pp/0err compile gate, but it remains live ledger/provenance until compactly packaged and independently checked. Agent/diagram-aid ledgers are finders rather than certification. SGA5 is not English-synchronized, index-audited, globally source-faithful, independently certified, or critical. SGA6 and SGA7 carry compression and source-check caveats. Deligne, Bianchi, Gordan, Steinitz, Maxwell, Gibbs, Ukrainian applied mathematics, and the non-European/multilingual mathematics records also contain substantial work, but status varies by paper, page range, table, and diagram. Weber has useful local Phase 2 German workpass evidence, and the active Volume I p1-p99 source gap-pass now reaches p76. The separate completed 20-page Volume I sample-cert audit failed as certification: §26/p90 and §164/p544 require full re-transcription, p400 and p580 content drops were fixed locally, 12 sample pages were clean, and §141-188 should be reverified page-by-page. This is local source-audit/workpass evidence, not whole-volume certification or English synchronization.

Partial streams and mixed shelves. Dedekind, Dirichlet, Gauss, Riemann, and Poincare have useful author records, but should be read package by package rather than as seamless author-complete editions. The classical algebra/arithmetic shelf and additional author cluster are staging/backstop shelves, not blanket quality claims.

OCR/support/provenance or currently unsafe draft lanes. EGA is a French-originals, OCR/support, upstream/community TeX, and partial English draft lane. It is useful for preservation and continuation, but not comparable to SGA's active source-audit workpass lane. Cayley is currently de-promoted: broad PDFs, TeX, unit indexes, and ZIPs are retained for salvage and future repair, but no Cayley range is currently promoted as source-faithful.

Noether local source-control/support head. The Noether author record now fronts the July 3 R685/R686/R687/R688 source-control/support refresh. R685 and R686 are no-patch source-support layers: R685 routes clean article-level GDZ PDFs for P40/P41 and records source-quality cautions for P42/P30, while R686 directly audits P41 against the clean GDZ article source and promotes no TeX patch. R687 is a narrow TeX-changing P40 repair: on printed p537 / cumulative line 19668 the displayed direct-sum formula begins with source `Z_\Omega`, not plain `Z`. R688 is a narrow TeX-changing P24 repair: on printed p234 / source PDF p239 the module-norm display uses source comma punctuation in `N(\frakG_{i-1},\frakM_{i-1})`, while neighboring ideal-norm vertical bars remain unchanged. The R688 repaired German cumulative compiles to 466 pages. Because the Noether record is at the 100-file ceiling, R685/R686/R687/R688 should be folded into a curated rollup rather than uploaded loose. This remains source-control/support material only, not a reader release, Noether closure, whole-corpus certification, 650+ source certification, multilingual synchronization, or a critical edition.

Infrastructure. This record, under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20393488, remains the bulk/raw/provenance landing page so author records do not need to re-upload multi-gigabyte raw archives every time. The workflow and replication packet documents the AI-run scan/OCR/source-witness/TeX/translation/audit/GitHub/Zenodo workflow and its current failure modes. A dedicated interlanguage/methodology lane now preserves Ukrainian/Russian/Interslavic, constructed-language, and terminology-governance apparatus; it is linguistics/methodology material, not a Noether reader release, native-speaker approval, term approval, mathematical source certification, language synchronization proof, or critical edition. A dedicated Lean/formalization sidecar lane now preserves useful Lean 4/mathlib-style candidate material for Noether, Steinitz, Weber, and Jordan; it is not source-fidelity certification, translation certification, page-completeness certification, or a critical edition.

Quality note. This landing page is not a critical edition, and no public record in this project should be read as a critical edition, critically complete edition, or mathematically certified edition unless a future record explicitly says that such certification has been completed. Words such as complete, source-checked, strict, or critical in older filenames may be inherited package labels or structural coverage labels. Verify citation-critical formulas, diagrams, tables, theorem statements, cross-references, and unusual notation against the source scans.

Corrections and contributions. Source comparisons, LaTeX fixes, translation corrections, and reader-facing issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.

Noether predecessor note. Earlier R574/R573/R572/R571/R570/R569 wording is historical beneath the current July 3 R685/R686/R687/R688 split. R574 remains an earlier Paper 30 p32 source-control repair; R573 remains an earlier Paper 40 source-style merge; R572/R571/R570/R569 remain older support/tail-control layers. They are predecessor/status history, not the current fronting baseline.

July 3 R687/SGA p480/Weber p76 correction. Current local public metadata now fronts Noether R685/R686/R687/R688, SGA5 p480 live-ledger caveats, and Weber Volume I p1-p76 active source gap-pass status. Older R574, SGA p428, and Weber sample-cert-only paragraphs in historical receipts are predecessor/status history, not the current fronting baseline.

2026-07-03 interlanguage branch status note. The imported Noether PC/interlanguage package-141 status clarification is methodology/status infrastructure only: selected-excerpt filename hits are metadata/template labels, not captured excerpts or source text; no translations, review returns, approvals, or readiness claims are implied.

2026-07-03 R689/R673/R690 Noether staging note. R689 is a no-patch anomaly/routing package; R673 Paper 13 packages are older-base source-fix inputs still awaiting forward merge; R690 is a local merge workspace only. Do not treat this as a new reader release or certification.
